item.title: Sparse Kernel Methods - Lagrange Multipliers
item.description: One of the significant limitations of learning algorithms based on non-linear kernels is that the kernel function $k(X_n, X_m)$ must be evaluated for all possible pairs $X_n$ and $X_m$ of training points. For us, it will be favourable that we shall look at kernel-based algorithms that have sparse solutions, so that predictions for new inputs depend only on the kernel function evaluated at a subset of the training data points. One of the most used sparse solution is support vector machine (SVM). An important property of support vector machines is that the determination of the model parameters corresponds to a convex optimization problem, and so any local solution is also a global optimum. It should be noted that the SVM is a decision machine and so does not provide posterior probabilities.
